---
title: "SLA Time-to-Done Breach Rate"
description: "Share of PSOM tickets that missed the time-to-done SLA."
---

The proportion of PSOM tickets that missed the "Time to done" SLA, based on the
latest snapshot.

This metric reflects how well the team is resolving tickets within the agreed
timeframe. It measures the whole ticket, including time spent escalated to
another team. Only tickets where the SLA clock started are included; tickets
with no clock are excluded.

## Calculation

From [`jira.psom_sla`](../../catalog/jira/psom_sla.qmd), filter
to the most recent `date` partition, to `sla = 'time_to_done'`, and to rows
where `breached` is not null (i.e., the clock started). Divide the count of
rows where `breached` is true by the total count of those rows.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_sla_tickets,
    SUM(CASE WHEN breached THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS breached_count,
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN breached THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE)
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS breach_rate
FROM jira.psom_sla
WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM jira.psom_sla)
  AND sla = 'time_to_done'
  AND breached IS NOT NULL;
```

## R

```r
psom_sla <- tbl(con, in_schema("jira", "psom_sla"))
latest_date <- psom_sla |> summarise(d = max(date, na.rm = TRUE)) |> pull(d)

psom_sla |>
  filter(
    as.Date(date) == as.Date(latest_date),
    sla == "time_to_done",
    !is.na(breached)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    total_sla_tickets = n(),
    breached_count    = sum(as.integer(breached), na.rm = TRUE),
    breach_rate       = sum(as.integer(breached), na.rm = TRUE) / as.double(n())
  )
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

The rate is a proportion between 0 and 1. Tickets whose
clock never started (null `breached`) are excluded from both numerator and
denominator. Check `total_sla_tickets` to understand the sample size underlying
the rate.

The goal is set per ticket (16, 24, 40 and 72 working hours all occur), so a
breach means the ticket missed its own target, not a shared one. Working hours
run 09:00 to 17:00, so a 40-hour goal is one working week. To compare how long
tickets took, use `elapsed_minutes` instead, which is populated from
2026-09-29.

A ticket that is still open and inside its goal is recorded as not breached
(`false`), the same as a ticket that met the SLA. The rate on a live snapshot
is therefore a lower bound: some of those open tickets may still breach before
they are resolved. It is most meaningful once the snapshot's tickets are
largely resolved.

## Alternative names

- time to done SLA breach rate
- resolution SLA compliance
- time-to-done SLA failure rate
